items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIV, List of Answers on Terminology 51:1
items.html: (To the question) What is the Life of the worlds? The Yesod of ZA is discerned by the name Joseph, which is the aspect of the Righteous that enters into him, namely the nine Sefirot of the direct light that he draws. However, he also includes the aspect of Benjamin, namely the aspect of the screens that raise the nine Sefirot of the returning light, for before ZA bestows the Mochin to the Nukva, those Mochin must be revealed in himself, and afterward he bestows them to his Nukva. Therefore it is necessary that he also has the aspect of Benjamin, who raises the nine Sefirot of the returning light, for without him there is no coupling in existence at all, as is known. And this is the secret that the Yesod is called Chai, to hint that it includes also the aspect of the screens of Benjamin, and therefore it itself raises nine Sefirot of the direct light from above downward and nine Sefirot of the returning light from below upward, which are numerically Chai. And for this reason the Yesod is called "the Life of the worlds," being Chai in the two worlds: first in the world of the male, namely that first it brings out the stature in its own Mochin in the secret of Chai, as above, which is the world of the male; and afterward it bestows that stature to the female, called the world of the female, and brings out there as well nine from above downward and nine from below upward, in the aspect of her own screens. And then ZA alone is discerned as the aspect of Joseph, and the female alone as the aspect of Benjamin, and between the two of them come out the eighteen second Sefirot. And this is the secret of "Chai Chai, they will praise You," namely Chai in the world of the male and Chai in the world of the female. (Item 77).
